_comment: English body for lerobot (robotics). Official README fetched 200 on 2026-11-07; unknowns kept explicit.

axes.model_access: LeRobot is not a model product; the official README lists no model provider list. Policy or model integration usually goes through user code and ecosystem integrations; this site records it as model/policy-agnostic (site judgement, verification limited to README).
axes.runtime: LeRobot is used as a library/framework in local processes, commonly via Python/C++ or the ROS ecosystem; it is not a hosted cloud service. Installation and platform support follow official README/docs and were not tested here.
axes.local_files: LeRobot reads and writes local configuration, scenes, models or data assets; file permissions and asset licences must be checked by the user. It does not manage training-data copyright or robot workspace safety for the user.
axes.background: Nodes or training processes can run in the background; shutdown continuation, distribution and failure recovery are outside this verification scope and must be checked against official deployment docs.
axes.tools: LeRobot provides command-line, plugin or ecosystem interfaces (such as ROS topics/services, simulation plugins, policy-training interfaces). MCP integration is not stated in the official README and is recorded as unknown.
axes.context: Not applicable: LeRobot is not a chat model and has no LLM context window; state is carried by configuration, scenes, node state or training checkpoints.
axes.permissions: Permissions follow the operating system and runtime environment; with robot hardware, device access, network and emergency-stop boundaries also need checking. The official README gives no unified permission model, and this was not tested here.
axes.fit: Fit: robot policy training and demonstration-data experiments. Not fit: unverified production deployment, safety certification or real-hardware guarantees.

unknowns:
- Mainland direct access to website/install sources and filing status were not tested in this pass.
- Upstream push/release cadence was not verified via API; lifecycle is unknown.
- MCP integration is not stated in the official README.
related: Another category: local model runner. If a policy needs local inference, read llama.cpp for format and quantisation boundaries.
